thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: Production inference clusters experiencing elevated tail latency and paging. p95 and p99 breached for streaming endpoints. Automated paging triggered. Notified on-call.

maria: I'm oncall, looking. seeing p99 spike ~5-6s on streaming routes, affecting a subset of customers. kicking off triage — please paste relevant dashboards/logs.

ajay: Grafana snapshots: query used: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`. p95 went from 120ms -> 1.1s, p99 from 300ms -> 5.2s. Streaming stalls correlate with high `kv_cache_evict_rate` and `kv_prefill_queue_depth`.

kevin: Observing slab eviction churn on nodes serving decode workers. Eviction rate spiked to ~1.2k/s. slab_utilization shows fragmentation -- lots of small free segments. suspect prefill traffic is filling cold keys and causing decode-to-prefill eviction imbalance.

sara: Can we confirm whether recent rollout changed prefill concurrency or cache slab sizing? I remember PR #462 changed prefill batcher default concurrency to 8 from 4.

ajay: Yes, that PR rolled out 3h ago to canary and then prod. Canary metrics showed slight increase in prefill throughput; prod pushed at ~+2h before spike. Timeline lines up.

maria: Ok. Immediate mitigation options: (A) throttle prefill concurrency via feature-flag on the gateway, (B) increase KV cache slab reservation for decode vs prefill, (C) temporarily route streaming to smaller-model fallback for affected customers.

kevin: I'm going to try (B) first: bump decode slab reservation by 15% on cluster group a-prod-1. If that reduces eviction pressure we get breathing room. If not, we'll flip (A).

maria: Do it and post command. I'll watch latency panels.

kevin: Running command:
```
# increase decode slab reservation
curl -s -X POST "https://config.internal/api/v1/cluster/a-prod-1/cache/sizes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"decode_reservation_pct": "0.15"}'
```
Patch applied. Restart not required.

ops-bot: config-applier: cache config update accepted for a-prod-1 by kevin. change_id=chg-20260312-778.

ajay: After ~2m, eviction rate dropped from 1200/s -> 220/s, prefill queue depth still elevated but not causing massive evictions. p99 started falling to ~900ms then ~450ms.

maria: Good. We're seeing p99 regress toward baseline. I'm going to enable prefill throttle as a defensive measure while we investigate the PR effects.

kevin: Throttling prefill via gate:
```
# set feature flag to limit prefill concurrency
curl -X POST https://ff.internal/flags/prefill_concurrency -d '{"value":4}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Flag applied.

ajay: p95 ~200ms, p99 ~320ms now. Streaming stalls cleared from dashboards. No more paging messages.

sara: Drafting customer-facing blurb: "We observed an elevated tail-latency incident starting 2026-03-12T14:05Z affecting streaming responses for ~6-12% of requests. Root cause: cache eviction pressure caused by recent prefill concurrency change causing imbalance between prefill and decode cache usage. Mitigation: adjusted cache reservations and throttled prefill; service performance restored. Postmortem to follow."

maria: Looks good. Add ETA for follow-up and mention impacted customers will receive targeted notification.

kevin: Quick notes for post-incident: correlate PR #462, add a safety circuit to automatically back off prefill concurrency if `kv_cache_evict_rate` > 500/s for 30s, add alert for `kv_prefill_vs_decode_free_ratio` to detect fragmentation, and add a rolling change validation that measures tail latency on streaming routes.

ajay: I created an alert runbook entry and linked dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/prefill-eviction. Also added a quick query to check prefill vs decode allocations: `sum(kv_prefill_alloc_bytes) / sum(kv_decode_alloc_bytes)` — currently trending >1.8 which is suspicious.

maria: Handoff: kevin will own followups. I'll continue on call for 20 more minutes then hand to next oncall. Action items assigned: kevin (root cause analysis + automated backoff), ajay (alert tuning + dashboards), sara (customer comms + targeted outreach), maria (postmortem + reviewer).

kevin: Taking it. I'll roll forward with a deeper heap/profile trace on decode workers and schedule a rollback of PR #462 if root cause confirmed.

maria: Thanks team — incident mitigated, monitoring closely. If anything regresses, re-open paging. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT update: SEV2 mitigated at 2026-03-12T15:08Z. Incident remains open for postmortem tracking and action items.
